pack.description: Listen to an Announcement — 40–85 word campus and academic announcements, two questions each.
pack.copyright_policy: Original synthetic content. No operational ETS item copied.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement made to students.

audio.speaker: Announcer
audio.text: Attention students registered for tomorrow's career workshop. Because the Student Center auditorium is being repaired, the workshop has been moved to Room 204 of the Business Building. The starting time remains ten o'clock. Please bring your student identification card for check-in, and arrive fifteen minutes early if you would like an individual résumé review.

questions.stem: Why is the announcement being made?
options: To announce a change of location
questions.explanation: The workshop moved to Room 204; the time remains the same.

questions.stem: What should students do if they want a résumé review?
options: Go to the Student Center first
questions.explanation: Arrive fifteen minutes early for an individual review.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement at the beginning of a class.

audio.speaker: Professor
audio.text: Before we start, a quick note about the midterm. Several of you asked whether calculators are allowed. They are, but only the basic models listed on the course page, not graphing calculators. Also, the exam will now cover chapters one through six rather than seven, since we didn't finish chapter seven in time. Review sessions are on Monday evening.

questions.stem: What change does the professor announce about the exam?
options: It has been moved to Monday
It will cover fewer chapters than planned
questions.explanation: Chapters one to six instead of seven, because chapter seven was not finished.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the calculators?
options: Students may not use any calculator
Some students may need to check whether their calculator is permitted
questions.explanation: Only models listed on the course page are allowed, so students should check theirs.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement on the university radio station.

audio.speaker: Announcer
audio.text: Congratulations to the university debate team, which won the regional championship last weekend after defeating twelve other universities. The team will represent the region at the national finals in April. To help cover travel costs, team members will be selling coffee and pastries outside the main library every morning next week. All proceeds go directly to the trip.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To recruit new debate team members
To report a team's success and ask for support
To advertise a new café in the library
To announce the results of the national finals
questions.explanation: It reports the regional win and promotes a fundraiser for the trip.

questions.stem: Why will the team be selling food?
options: To raise money for travel to the finals
To attract students to the library
To pay for a new coach
questions.explanation: Proceeds help cover travel costs to the national finals.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement in a university library.

audio.speaker: Announcer
audio.text: Good evening. The library will close in thirty minutes. Please begin gathering your belongings and bring any books you wish to borrow to the front desk within the next fifteen minutes, as the checkout system shuts down before closing. Group study rooms must be vacated now so that they can be cleaned. Thank you, and good night.

questions.stem: Why should students go to the front desk soon?
options: Because checkout stops before the library closes
To book a study room for tomorrow
Because the desk is being cleaned
questions.explanation: The checkout system shuts down before closing, so books must be brought within fifteen minutes.

questions.stem: What are students in group study rooms asked to do?
questions.explanation: Rooms "must be vacated now" for cleaning.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement made by a department administrator.

audio.speaker: Administrator
audio.text: A reminder to all graduate students: travel grant applications for spring conferences are due on March first. This year, priority will go to students presenting their own research rather than attending only. Because the budget is smaller than last year's, awards are capped at five hundred dollars, so please also apply to the Graduate School's fund if your costs are higher.

questions.stem: Which applicants are most likely to receive funding?
options: Students who will present their own research
Students with the highest travel costs
questions.explanation: Priority goes to students presenting their own research.

questions.stem: Why does the administrator mention the Graduate School's fund?
options: Because the department fund may not cover all expenses
Because the department fund has been closed
Because only first-year students can apply to it
questions.explanation: Awards are capped at five hundred dollars, so students with higher costs need another source.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement made in a residence hall.

audio.speaker: Resident advisor
audio.text: Hi everyone. The fire alarm system will be tested on Thursday between ten and noon. The alarm may sound several times, but you do not need to leave the building unless you hear the alarm together with a message telling you to evacuate. Please make sure nothing is blocking the hallway exits before Thursday.

questions.stem: When should residents leave the building on Thursday?
options: Only if a spoken evacuation message accompanies the alarm
questions.explanation: Leave only if the alarm comes with a message telling you to evacuate.

questions.stem: What are residents asked to do before the test?
options: Clear the exits in the hallways
questions.explanation: Make sure nothing blocks the hallway exits.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement at the start of a science lecture.

audio.speaker: Professor
audio.text: Before we begin today, I want to recognize Daniel Kim, a student in this course, whose research on soil bacteria has just been accepted for publication. That is a rare achievement for an undergraduate. Daniel has agreed to give a short talk about the project in our last session, so start thinking about questions you might ask him.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the announcement?
options: To introduce a guest lecturer from another university
To recruit students for a research project
questions.explanation: She recognizes Daniel's research being accepted for publication.

questions.stem: What are students asked to do?
options: Prepare questions for a future talk
questions.explanation: "Start thinking about questions you might ask him" for the last session.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement on a campus bus.

audio.speaker: Driver
audio.text: Attention passengers. Due to road construction on Main Street, this bus will not stop at the Science Center today. Passengers for the Science Center should get off at the next stop, the Arts Building, and walk about five minutes east. Regular service will resume tomorrow morning. We apologize for the inconvenience.

questions.stem: Why will the bus not stop at the Science Center?
options: There is construction on the road

questions.stem: What should passengers going to the Science Center do?
options: Stay on until the end of the route
Get off at the Arts Building and walk
Take a taxi from Main Street
questions.explanation: Get off at the Arts Building and walk five minutes east.

exercises.context: Listen to an announcement made by a course instructor.

audio.speaker: Instructor
audio.text: I've had a number of questions about the use of AI tools in the final paper. To be clear: you may use them to check grammar or to brainstorm, but any text they generate must not appear in your paper, and you must describe how you used them in a short appendix. Papers without that appendix will be returned ungraded.

questions.stem: According to the instructor, which use of AI tools is allowed?
options: Summarizing the readings in the final text
questions.explanation: Checking grammar and brainstorming are allowed; generated text must not appear.

questions.stem: What will happen to a paper submitted without the appendix?
options: It will lose a few points
It will be returned without a grade
It will be checked by software
It will be accepted if no AI was used
questions.explanation: "Papers without that appendix will be returned ungraded."
